Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: ONE transparent PNG animated character atlas for the Agumon evolution line in a 2D mobile RPG, polished 1990s Digimon Adventure anime with clean expressive cel shading adapted to compact chibi game sprites. EXACTLY SIX COLUMNS and NINE ROWS of equally sized cells (54 separate full-body poses), portrait 2:3 image with equal square grid cells, transparent alpha in all gaps. No cell lines, captions, text or shadows. Each character centered at a shared foot baseline in its cell, generous clear gaps; nothing may cross cell boundaries. Identity must match Digimon anime:
Rows 1-3 AGUMON: small friendly orange dinosaur, green eyes, big snout, round cream-yellow belly, three white claws per hand and foot, stubby tail.
Rows 4-6 GREYMON: muscular orange tyrannosaur dinosaur, blue body stripes, dark brown horned skull helmet with a central nose horn and two rear horns, powerful hind feet and tail; no armor elsewhere.
Rows 7-9 METALGREYMON: orange Greymon with metallic silver cyborg helmet and armored left arm, blue torn bat wings, exposed chest missile hatch panels, striped orange body, long tail. Clearly recognizable MetalGreymon, not the blue Virus version.

SIX COLUMNS for every row: (1) relaxed neutral ready/idle with all feet planted, mouth closed; (2) walking, left foot forward/right foot back; (3) walking, right foot forward/left foot back (different leg silhouette from column 2); (4) normal melee attack anticipation, crouch and pull arm back; (5) normal melee attack strike, lunge with open jaw and one claw slashing forward, feet still inside cell; (6) special skill casting/release, braced stance, open mouth breathing attack, glowing orange eyes, NO fireball or aura drawn outside body. Show real anatomical pose changes, not merely translated copies. Keep exact same character colors, body proportions and outline thickness in every pose for a given form. Fixed slightly elevated RPG camera. Same clean detailed anime style as Taichi sheet. True transparent background, all 54 cells populated, no UI or logos.
